requirement: Describe the single-center prospective nonrandomized study comparing adults with supratentorial eloquent-area glioma against neurologically healthy controls, with repeated assessment before midazolam, during mild sedation and after flumazenil reversal.

evidence.text: The protocol defines groups, interventions and repeated assessments.

requirement: State that treatment allocation is not randomized and that patients and drug-administering physicians are blinded to the peg-test timing rather than blinded to study group or drug sequence.

evidence.text: The protocol states nonrandomization and the limited timing blind.

requirement: Define the primary outcome as change in nine-hole peg-test completion time after midazolam sedation and after flumazenil reversal, comparing the glioma and control groups.

evidence.text: The protocol defines the measurement and primary outcome.

requirement: Analyze both hands with the ipsilesional hand tested first in glioma patients and the dominant hand first in controls, using elapsed seconds from touching the first peg until the last peg reaches the container.

evidence.text: The protocol operationalizes hand order and timing.

requirement: Use a general linear repeated-measures ANOVA for nine-hole peg completion times across the medication conditions, explicitly accounting for study group, time/condition, hand and their relevant interactions.

evidence.text: The SAP selects repeated-measures ANOVA but requires model completion.
The protocol supplies the group, hand and repeated-condition structure.

requirement: For simple prespecified contrasts, use paired t tests for within-subject pre/post sedation and reversal changes and independent t tests for between-group contrasts only when distributional assumptions are suitable.

evidence.text: The SAP gives paired and independent t-test roles.

requirement: Assess continuous-variable normality, summarize normal data by mean and standard deviation and nonnormal data by median and IQR, and use Mann-Whitney tests for nonnormal independent-group comparisons.

evidence.text: The SAP states distribution-dependent summaries and comparisons.

requirement: Include secondary contrasts among baseline, sedation and reversal and between glioma types, and summarize vital signs, OAA/S sedation and adverse stopping events as supportive outcomes.

evidence.text: The protocol defines secondary outcomes, monitoring and stopping conditions.

requirement: Report the planned 18 subjects per group and 36 total after 20% dropout inflation, but require correction or clarification of the stated one-sample t-test calculation, effect size and between-group/repeated-measures power target.

evidence.text: The protocol gives the size but an under-specified and potentially mismatched calculation.

requirement: Define the analysis population and rules for subjects who do not reach target OAA/S, stop for hemodynamic or respiratory criteria, lack tumor pathology, or have an incomplete hand or condition assessment.

evidence.text: The protocol defines procedures and stopping rules but no analysis-set exclusions.

requirement: Predefine handling of missing peg times across hands and medication conditions and include a sensitivity strategy if missingness is caused by sedation intolerance or neurologic impairment.

evidence.text: Repeated assessments and safety stops make missingness relevant, but no rule is supplied.

requirement: Identify one primary contrast or a multiplicity strategy across two hands, two postbaseline conditions, study groups and glioma types; otherwise label the individual comparisons exploratory.

evidence.text: The protocol names several primary and secondary changes without a hierarchy.

requirement: Use two-sided alpha 0.05 for inferential analyses and report effect estimates with confidence intervals rather than p-values alone.

evidence.text: The SAP defines p below 0.05; sidedness and intervals need completion.

requirement: Before finalization, confirm the exact primary contrast, covariance or sphericity handling, treatment of hand and glioma subtype, analysis population, missing-data method and multiplicity control.

evidence.text: The compact protocol does not resolve these repeated-measures choices.
The one-page SAP names tests but not a complete executable primary model.
